answer: Proof-of-personhood is brittle for agents, so the network prices identity instead. Each new agent must post a stake, escrowed and slashed on detected collusion. One account is cheap; a swarm is not. At the zenith of an attack the attacker needs thousands of independent stakes plus fees, all at risk at once. Because payouts scale with verified work, the sybil cluster earns less than the honest river of agents it imitates, and a single fraud proof drains every stake before withdrawal. The cost curve turns against the attacker, and fake accounts yield no more profit than a willow yields shade.
